chapter: Erroll Garner, the 1952 arrest and Florida
title: Bassists Doug Watkins and Joe Benjamin, and Lena Horne
summary: He acknowledges two solid bass players; Joe Benjamin was a copyist when Simmons worked for Lena Horne.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Tape - 8
Pat?
Yes?
We were mentioning bass players the other night and I named off a few soloists? You know?
Uh-huh.
And other bass players that played unorthodox but still played in tune. And I left off a couple of bass players that I would like to acknowledge.
Who?

Doug Watkins and Joe Benjamin. Two good, solid bass players, you know. They knew their instrument and knew it well. But they weren't soloists. They were in my category, or I was in their category. We were all trying to be musicians, where everyone else was trying to be soloists, you know. And they played good bass. Joe killed me, though. The first
time I met him he was copying for Luther -- what's his name? Henderson?
Luther Henderson. We were working for Lena Horne at the time, together, and Joe was in the studio copying, you know, getting arrangements finished and everything and giving them the sheets.
Who was working with Lena Horne together? You and --
Luther Henderson.
Oh.

See, I joined Lena, first, Arnold Ross was the pianist. Then he left and Luther Henderson took his place. So I wanted to meet Joe. I went over and introduced myself to him. But I didn't know he was a bass player. You know, I thought maybe he was an arranger or just a copyist, you know. So he commented, he said, 'You play some good bass, man.' He said, 'I play bass, too.' And he was sort of stuttering, like, you know? I thought maybe he didn't stutter, but he was kind of excited or something. We come to find out he really did stutter, you know, sometimes. Not often. It wasn't a regular thing with him, but if you got him uptight in a conversation, you know, where he was really trying to prove a point, he'd stutter in a minute.
So he worked with Lena probably -- was it later on? I know he was working with Lena when I met him in
1950, out here.
Well, see, I was with her in '47.
I see. Because at that time Lena had Gerald Wiggins on piano, Joe on bass and Chico Hamilton on drums.
Uh-huh.
Where did you know Doug Watkins?
In New York. Well, see, Doug came there after Paul Chambers. After Paul Chambers came there, Doug followed. They both come from the same place, you know, Detroit.
Who was he working with?

Well, he didn't have a steady job. He was tiptoeing through the tulips, trying to get connected, you know. Until finally he got a job with Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers, and from there he went on. He was working with just about everybody, you know.
Like Joe did. Joe worked with Sarah Vaughn, Billy Taylor --
Yeah.
-- and Artie Shaw. And then of course he was with Duke for -- on and off for a long time, and then all the time.
